ThingDef.label: the second king's tomb
ThingDef.description: His son. Nineteen when it came to him, which it did the same week it came off his father, because nobody could think of a reason to wait.\n\nSeven years. The band on the lid is cut by the same hand as the first king's, and it is the last one that is.

ThingDef.label: the third king's tomb
ThingDef.description: A cousin, and by all accounts a decent one. Six years.\n\nHe won a war whose cause nobody wrote down, on the grounds that everyone alive already knew it. Nobody alive knows it.

ThingDef.label: the fourth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Six years. She built the east road, the good one, the one that is still there and still carries carts.\n\nShe is not on it anywhere. No milestone, no bridge, no gate. It was finished the year she died and the naming of it never happened.

ThingDef.label: the fifth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Five years. He wrote the laws on inheritance and water rights that clerks in three kingdoms still copy out, usually without knowing whose they were.\n\nThe lid has been opened and closed again at some point. Somebody checked.

ThingDef.label: the sixth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: The only one who tried to give it away. Four years.\n\nHe got as far as the gate of this barrow with it in his hands, and then he turned around and went home wearing it, and he never spoke about the walk back.

ThingDef.label: the seventh king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Five years. She asked it for a harvest and it gave her eleven at once: the grain came up in a single season, all of it, everywhere, and the fields have never been right since.\n\nShe asked for nothing else afterward. It made no difference.

ThingDef.label: the eighth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Three years, and used up at thirty-one, which the court recorded as a wasting illness.\n\nThe court physician's notes survive in the reliquary at the monastery. They describe a man in perfect health who was running out.

ThingDef.label: the ninth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Four years. He kept a diary every day of his reign, which is more than any of the others managed.\n\nEvery entry after the second year is in a hand that is very nearly his.

ThingDef.label: the tenth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Three years. She won every argument she ever entered, including the ones she had alone, in a locked room, out loud.\n\nHer council stopped bringing her questions in the second year. Not out of fear. There was simply no point.

ThingDef.label: the eleventh king's tomb
ThingDef.description: Two years. The shortest of them, and the only one anybody wept for.\n\nHe was nineteen, he was good at it, and the household who buried him carved the lid themselves rather than send out for a mason.

ThingDef.label: the twelfth king's tomb
ThingDef.description: The last one. She sent the crown out of her hall in five directions on five roads, with five riders who knew what they were carrying, and then she barred the doors and set the hall alight with herself inside it, so that there would be nothing left for it to come back to.\n\nThis box holds what they could carry out of the ashes. It is not heavy.
